title: Private PAC sample complexity from VC and Littlestone dimensions
formal: Do there exist universal integers \(A,k\ge1\) such that every nonempty finite Boolean concept class \(\mathcal C\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal X}\) on a nonempty finite domain \(\mathcal X\), with \(v=\operatorname{VC}(\mathcal C)\ge1\) and \(d=\operatorname{LD}(\mathcal C)\ge1\), has a positive integer sample size \[m\le A\bigl(1+v+\log^{*}d\bigr)^{k}\] and a possibly improper learner \(L\) that is \((1,1/(100m^{2}))\)-differentially private and realizes the following PAC guarantee? For every distribution \(D\) on \(\mathcal X\) and every target \(h^{*}\in\mathcal C\), when \(L\) receives \(m\) independent samples \((x_i,h^{*}(x_i))\) with \(x_i\sim D\), its output \(\widehat h\) satisfies \[\Pr\!\left[\Pr_{x\sim D}[\widehat h(x)\ne h^{*}(x)]\le1/10\right]\ge9/10.\] The same \(m,L\) must work for all \(D,h^{*}\) for the chosen class. Their choice can depend on the complete class, but \(A,k\) cannot. Computation is unrestricted. This is the previously selected concrete polynomial-overhead version of the source question; the constant accuracy, confidence and sample-dependent privacy parameters are editorial specifications, not parameter values asserted in the source.
why: The theorem characterizing whether private learning is possible leaves an enormous quantitative gap. This question asks whether the extra data needed for privacy is controlled by ordinary statistical complexity and an exceptionally slowly growing function of sequential complexity. A positive answer would put a uniform bound on that privacy overhead across all finite concept classes.

progress.text: Lower and upper results establish the equivalence of finite Littlestone dimension and approximate private PAC learnability, as summarized in Theorem 1 of the 2026 source.
Yan’s Theorem 1 gives a nearly optimal private sample bound for VC-dimension-one classes; the result includes an explicit accuracy, confidence and privacy-parameter formula.
Lyu’s Theorem 2 improves the general private PAC bound to a fifth power of Littlestone dimension up to the stated logarithmic and privacy/accuracy factors; the paper appears at STOC 2026.
The COLT 2026 invited open problem explicitly proposes a polynomial VC/log-star-LD upper bound and states that the general characterization remains open.

Checked the full COLT 2026 source, Lyu’s theorem and publication record, and Yan’s parameter-explicit theorem. A bounded later-work search found no proof or refutation of the universal polynomial-overhead target.

context_blocks.text: Nonprivate PAC learning at constant accuracy and confidence has sample complexity governed by VC dimension. Approximate private learnability instead has a qualitative connection to finite Littlestone dimension. This equivalence says that a finite sample bound exists; it does not identify how large the bound must be.

For finite classes, the 2026 source summarizes a lower scale \(\Omega(v+\log^{*}d)\) and upper scales \(\min\{O(\log|\mathcal C|),\widetilde O(d^{5})\}\), suppressing privacy and learning parameters. The proposed bound depends polynomially on \(v\) and \(\log^{*}d\), so replacing \(d\) by another fixed power does not answer it. The source presents this as one concrete formulation following its broader characterization question.

Lyu’s improved PAC learner has a bound \(\widetilde O(d^{5}\log(1/\delta)/(\varepsilon\alpha))\), with the remaining confidence and logarithmic factors specified in the paper. Its dependence on \(d\) is polynomial but is still much larger than a polynomial in \(\log^{*}d\). The result was published at STOC 2026; the checked detailed theorem is in the 2025 author manuscript.

Yan proves a nearly matching iterated-logarithmic bound when \(v=1\), including an improper learner and explicit parameter dependence. The 2026 problem paper also discusses thresholds, rectangles and halfspaces where the privacy overhead is relatively small. These positive special cases do not supply a bound uniform over unbounded VC dimension.

The card retains the earlier editorial normalization \(\varepsilon=1\), error \(1/10\), failure probability \(1/10\), and \(\delta=1/(100m^{2})\). In particular, \(\delta\) is tied to the actual sample size, rather than silently treated as a fixed constant while \(m\) grows. The source suppresses these parameters, so its displayed summary bounds are context rather than claims that every hidden factor is independent of this normalization.

definitions: A concept is a binary function; the learner knows \(\mathcal X\) and \(\mathcal C\). The VC dimension \(v\) is the largest cardinality of a subset \(S\subseteq\mathcal X\) on which the restrictions of \(\mathcal C\) realize every binary labeling. A complete binary tree of depth \(r\) has an instance point at each internal node and its two outgoing edges labeled 0 and 1. It is shattered by \(\mathcal C\) if every root-to-leaf edge-label sequence is produced by one fixed concept on that path's instance points. The Littlestone dimension \(d\) is the greatest shattered depth. For \(z\ge1\), \(\log^{*}z\) is the least number of successive base-two logarithms needed to obtain a value at most one; in particular \(\log^{*}1=0\). The dimension-zero case is excluded only to avoid a logarithm convention: on a fixed nonempty domain such a class contains a single distinct concept and has a data-independent exact predictor. A learner is an arbitrary probability kernel from \((\mathcal X\times\{0,1\})^m\) to the finite set \(\{0,1\}^{\mathcal X}\). It need not return a member of \(\mathcal C\). For every pair of labeled sample lists \(S,S'\) differing at one position and every subset \(E\) of output hypotheses, require \[\Pr[L(S)\in E]\le e\Pr[L(S')\in E]+1/(100m^{2}).\] Privacy holds even on samples not realizable by the class. The sample size is chosen before the target and distribution; the probability in the PAC guarantee includes both independently drawn examples and the learner's randomness. There are no runtime or representation bounds, and no uniform program across classes is required. The integer-power bound is equivalent to an unspecified universal polynomial in \(1+v\) and \(1+\log^{*}d\). A finite class on an arbitrary domain can be reduced to the finite domain of distinct label vectors \((h(x))_{h\in\mathcal C}\), of which there are at most \(2^{|\mathcal C|}\); both dimensions and these unrestricted learning/privacy requirements are preserved. Thus the finite-domain convention introduces no additional sample-complexity restriction on finite classes.
answer_criterion: Give a Lean-checked proof of the universal polynomial bound or its logical negation under the exact privacy and PAC conventions above. A positive answer must supply, for every class, a sample size and private learner satisfying the guarantee simultaneously for all targets and distributions. A negative answer must show that for every proposed pair of universal integers \(A,k\), some finite class admits no such learner at any positive integer sample size within the proposed bound. Computational lower bounds, proper-learning obstructions that disappear for improper learners, or a result only for one fixed VC dimension do not refute the statement.

importance.reason: Seeks a quantitative sample-complexity characterization of private learnability in terms of two basic dimensions, with consequences across hypothesis classes.

sentences: A private PAC learner must predict a Boolean concept accurately while protecting every individual labeled example.
The card asks for sample size polynomial in VC dimension and the iterated logarithm of Littlestone dimension for every finite class.
It retains fixed accuracy and confidence and privacy slack shrinking quadratically with the actual sample size.
The latest checked general upper bound is polynomial in Littlestone dimension itself, while the proposed much smaller dependence is known in important special cases.
A solution must prove the universal bound or a superpolynomial obstruction for unrestricted improper private learners, with its full quantifiers checked in Lean.
